subject: microbiology
title: Fried-Egg Colonies, Cold Agglutinins and Ureaplasma

steps.tx: **Fried egg colonies** are the classical growth form of Mycoplasma on enriched agar: a dense central core grows down into the medium while a thinner translucent periphery spreads on the surface. Colonies are tiny and require low-power microscopy. Mycoplasma pneumoniae may instead show granular colonies, so the fried egg image is a genus clue rather than a universal appearance for every species.
steps.say: A tiny colony with a dense centre and pale rim is the classic Mycoplasma postcard.

left.title: Colony features
points: Dense opaque centre embedded in agar
Thin translucent peripheral zone
Often only tens to hundreds of micrometres
Viewed with a dissecting microscope

right.title: Identification aids
points: Dienes stain retains blue colonies
No reversion to walled bacterial forms
Requires sterols and enriched media
Molecular testing now dominates clinical diagnosis

steps.tx: Mycoplasmas are bounded by a **sterol containing cell membrane** rather than a wall. They are pleomorphic because there is no rigid sacculus. Their small genomes force dependence on host-like nutrients in culture. The absence of a wall also means vancomycin, cephalosporins and penicillins are intrinsically useless. Resistance must instead arise against protein synthesis or DNA gyrase targets, such as macrolide binding site mutations.
steps.say: A sterol membrane without a wall explains Mycoplasma shape, culture demands and drug resistance.

left.title: Structural consequences
points: Pleomorphic cells and colonies
Osmotic fragility compared with walled bacteria
Not visible meaningfully on Gram stain
Sterol required in artificial medium

right.title: Therapeutic consequences
points: Beta lactams have no wall target
Macrolides target 50S ribosome
Doxycycline targets 30S ribosome
Fluoroquinolones target DNA enzymes in selected species

steps.tx: **Cold agglutinins** typically appear during the second week of Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection. At low temperature, IgM crosslinks red cells, and the sample visibly clumps at room or refrigerator temperature but disperses at 37 degrees Celsius. Most patients have no major haemolysis, yet high titres and strong thermal amplitude can cause anaemia and peripheral ischaemic symptoms. The test is supportive and not specific.
steps.say: Clumping that disappears on warming is the bedside physics of cold agglutinins.

nodes.label: IgM crosslinks red cell I antigen

steps.tx: **Ureaplasma** species split urea and produce ammonia, a property that separates them from other mycoplasmas. Ureaplasma urealyticum and Ureaplasma parvum colonise the lower genital tract frequently, but can cause urethritis, chorioamnionitis associations, neonatal respiratory disease and hyperammonaemia syndromes in profoundly immunocompromised transplant recipients. Detection by PCR does not automatically prove disease because colonisation is common.
steps.say: Ureaplasma detection needs clinical context because genital colonisation is common.

left.title: Biology
points: Urease generates ammonia for energy
Tiny colonies on special A8 agar
U urealyticum and U parvum distinguished molecularly
No cell wall, therefore beta lactam resistant

right.title: Disease associations
points: Non gonococcal urethritis
Neonatal pneumonia and meningitis in preterm infants
Invasive disease after transplantation
Hyperammonaemia from systemic infection in rare cases

steps.tx: **Mycoplasma hominis** is a genital mycoplasma associated with bacterial vaginosis ecology, postpartum fever, pelvic infection, surgical wound infection and bacteraemia after transplantation or urinary instrumentation. It is intrinsically resistant to macrolides that target a ribosomal site it does not share, whereas doxycycline and fluoroquinolones are usually active. It may form pinprick colonies on blood agar and be overlooked as diphtheroid-like contamination.
steps.say: M hominis reminds us that genital mycoplasmas do not all share M pneumoniae drug patterns.

left.title: Settings
points: Postpartum and post abortion fever
Renal transplant wound infection
Pelvic inflammatory processes
Extragenital abscess after bacteraemia

right.title: Laboratory clues
points: Arginine metabolism
Tiny translucent colonies after prolonged incubation
Fails to grow as expected on routine media
PCR or sequencing from sterile sites helps

steps.tx: **Mycoplasma genitalium** is a sexually transmitted species with established roles in urethritis, cervicitis and pelvic inflammatory disease. It grows extremely slowly, so NAAT is the only practical routine diagnostic. Macrolide resistance mutations are common in many populations and fluoroquinolone resistance is increasing. Resistance-guided sequential therapy is preferred where molecular resistance testing exists, and test of cure is important because symptoms can lag behind microbiological failure.
steps.say: M genitalium is a NAAT diagnosis whose therapy increasingly follows resistance genotype.

left.title: Clinical features
points: Persistent or recurrent urethritis
Cervicitis and pelvic pain
Often coinfected or confused with chlamydia
Extremely slow culture makes it impractical

right.title: Treatment principles
points: Test macrolide resistance where available
Avoid single dose azithromycin when resistance likely
Moxifloxacin for selected resistant infections
Perform test of cure after several weeks
